subject: Priority rationing appeal — Aurora AI dedicated capacity
messages:
From: Sofia Moreno <sofia.moreno@auroraai.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@auroraai.com
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity commitment for Q4

Hi Jordan & Laura,

Thanks again for the detailed run-through yesterday. We are preparing our Q4 launch plan and need to lock in a dedicated capacity reservation for our realtime inference workloads. The ask from our engineering team is a guaranteed 120 concurrent GPU slots (p95 8k seq) for the initial two-week launch burst, then 40 reserved slots steady-state.

I know Redwood has a tranche model — can you confirm whether a short, guaranteed burst like this can be accommodated without harming other customers, and what the expected lead time is for committing the tranche? We have an SOW attached (Aurora_SOW_v3.pdf) and a forecast (Capacity_Forecast_Q4.xlsx).

This is time-sensitive; procurement needs indicative capacity and risk controls by Aug 24.

Best,
Sofia Moreno
Head of Platform
Aurora AI

[Attachment: Aurora_SOW_v3.pdf (pdf)]
[Attachment: Capacity_Forecast_Q4.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Moreno <sofia.moreno@auroraai.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity commitment for Q4

Sofia — thanks for the materials. Quick summary: we can usually support a burst like that through a mix of reserved tranche + short-term preemptible overlay, but the guarantee level you request (120 concurrent guaranteed for two weeks) is non-trivial and will touch our committed pool for the region.

Next steps I propose:
- Internal capacity check with allocations team (cc'ing Ben) to see preemption impact and existing tranche commitments.
- If we can only offer a partial guarantee, propose a hybrid: 60 guaranteed + 60 on priority overlay with rollover credits if preempted.
- If that isn't acceptable, we can offer a firm date-specific carve (requires approval from capacity ops and may require short-term rebalancing).

I will loop in Ben for adjudication and Laura for commercial implications. Targeting an internal decision by Monday EOD Aug 24.

Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: Priority_Rules_Digest.docx (docx)]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 23 Aug 2026 08:31:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity commitment for Q4

Team — reviewed Aurora's forecast. Key constraints: we have another tranche booking (DEAL-1279) with a high-priority SLA overlapping the same window; that deal's contractually guaranteed p95 capacity is 80 slots. If we carve 120 to Aurora, we must either: push DEAL-1279 into a partial preemptible overlay during their low-traffic windows (risky) or consume additional unallocated GPUs from the spare pool and trigger cross-regional migration which increases latency for both customers.

Options (rapid):
1) Offer Aurora a staged guarantee: 60 guaranteed + 60 priority overlay. Provide them with "burst credit" mitigation (credits if preempted).
2) Offer full 120 guaranteed but only for a 3-day hard carve; otherwise 60 guaranteed for two weeks. This preserves schedule for DEAL-1279 and reduces long tail impact.
3) If Aurora insists on an all-or-nothing guarantee for two weeks, escalate to leadership for a temporary tranche reallocation and compensation plan.

I recommend option 1 unless Aurora will accept a shorter guaranteed window.

Ben Carter
VP, Customer Success Operations

[Internal note: will need sign-off from Laura on concession credits. Rishi: ledger/tally impact?]

From: Sofia Moreno <sofia.moreno@auroraai.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Chen <alex.chen@auroraai.com>, procurement@auroraai.com
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 07:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity commitment for Q4

Jordan/Ben — appreciate the quick analysis. Aurora's product team is firm on the two-week window; the launch has hard dates tied to a marketing campaign. The staged model is workable if there's a firm SLA for the first 48 hours (we can't accept preemption during launch peak). Can you provide explicit fallback guarantees and a compensation model (credits + increased priority for recovery) if preemption occurs during launch?

If you can supply a short hard carve for the first 48 hours and then the staged 60/60 split, I think procurement will sign. We can be flexible on price if Redwood can commit to that hybrid approach.

Thanks,
Sofia

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 17:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Priority rationing appeal — Aurora AI dedicated capacity

All — after quick sync w/ finance and allocations: we can approve a hybrid commitment for Aurora with the following commercial/operational guardrails:

1) Hard carve: 80 guaranteed GPUs for the first 48 hours of the launch window (to meet their peak SLA).
2) Follow-on: 40 guaranteed reserved slots for the subsequent two-week period + 40 priority overlay (total 80 capable). The overlay will be preemptible outside their peak windows.
3) Compensation: if >5% of the reserved tokens are preempted during the 48-hour hard carve, Aurora receives a 25% service credit for the burst and automatic priority recovery for the next 72 hours.
4) Escalation clause: any further request to convert overlay to guaranteed for more than 72 continuous hours requires leadership-level approval and a one-time tranche reallocation fee.

Ben: please prepare the capacity accounting change and the proposed credit clause language for the amendment to the SOW. Jordan: convey to Aurora and get procurement's written acceptance.

Laura Bennett
Head of Commercials & Partnerships
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: Capacity_Forecast_Q4.xlsx (referenced for numbers)]
